finding: The non-primary rationale reads: IndiaCode watermark, so the bytes are not the e-Gazette original; no C4 class covers a watermarked re-host; the C4 India Code class is for scans. This is imprecise. The C4 Act 37/1992 row (f11d443e, PRIMARY_GAZETTE_GOVERNMENT_HOSTED_SCAN) already records 'India Code watermarks served PDFs, so bytes are host-specific', so the watermark alone does not separate the two cases. What does separate them is that TRA is born-digital (vector text and embedded fonts on all 15 pages; producer iTextSharp) and carries an embedded signature whose ByteRange [0 577400 600412 8230] ends at byte 608,642 of the 637,026-byte held file, which has a single %%EOF. The signature therefore cannot cover the held bytes as a whole (structural observation, not a cryptographic check). The retrieval record S-REVA-016 also calls the file a 'Gazette scan', which conflicts with the C5 text-layer class and with C6. D1 shows remaining_gaps 'none recorded' for TRA although its class is reserved.

recommended_disposition: Restate the rationale with the precise distinguishing facts and the C4 watermark precedent, and keep the class reserved for the owner.
